title: How to Photograph Clothing for an AI Model Shoot
author: Muhammad, Founder of SetlesStudio
excerpt: See how to photograph clothing for an AI model shoot with a real plum two-piece set, from the original flat lay to the full-length model image and neckline close-up.
metaTitle: How to Photograph Clothing for an AI Model Shoot | SetlesStudio
metaDescription: Prepare sharp clothing photos for an AI model shoot. Compare a plum outfit’s flat lay, full-length model photo and neckline detail, then copy the shoot brief.
body: A scalloped neckline can look like a smooth diagonal in a full-length photo. A close-up shows the curves, but leaves the shopper guessing how the whole outfit looks. Before you photograph a garment for an AI model shoot, decide which questions each picture needs to answer. ## Start with the whole garment Lay the garment on a plain surface near a window with soft, even light. Hold your phone parallel to the garment and leave a little space beyond the cuffs and hem. Straighten accidental folds while keeping intentional gathers and pleats. For a matching set, take one picture of both pieces together and leave a gap so the waistband and the hem of the top are visible. Turn the garment over if you want to show the back on the model. The front can show where a shoulder strap begins. Only the back tells the studio whether it crosses, ties, or runs straight down. ## Give the defining detail its own photo Move closer and tap the detail on your screen to focus. For embroidery, include a nearby seam so the studio can see where the motif belongs. For an asymmetric neckline, include both shoulders in one reference before moving closer to the edge. Check the saved photo at full size. If the scallops or stitches run together, retake that shot while you still have the garment in front of you. Send the original files at full resolution. ## Studio case study: a plum top and matching leggings The distinguishing feature of this two-piece set is the scalloped edge running across one shoulder. Here are the product reference and two AI model images from our studio gallery. Each answers a different question. ### What does the original garment look like? Original product reference. Follow the neckline from one shoulder to the other, then look at where the top ends relative to the leggings. ### How do the pieces look together? AI model image, full-length view. Both pieces are visible in one frame, giving shoppers a sense of the outfit’s proportions. Use your garment measurements and size chart for sizing decisions. ### What makes this top recognizable? AI model image, detail view. Compare the direction and shape of the scalloped edge with the flat lay. Try the same comparison on a phone at normal viewing size. ## A photo brief you can copy “Please show the top and leggings together in one full-length studio image. For the second image, frame both shoulders closely enough that shoppers can see the scalloped neckline on a phone. Use the flat lay as the reference for the shape of the edge and the plum color.” For your own brief, replace “scalloped neckline” with the feature that makes your garment recognizable. If you sell a reversible jacket, photograph both sides. If you sell trousers with a hidden zip pocket, send one picture with the zip open. That small choice gives the studio a detail it can verify and the shopper a reason to look closer.
